member: Marcus - Vibration Control and Damping Specialist
message:
Elena, Priya, Tomas, to add damping without changing the deck look I propose a hidden mass-spring-damper unit hung under the deck at midspan where the first bending motion is largest, described as the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, a secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) (C2) and shown in the under-deck layout sketch (E25). This follows the Den Hartog TMD principle reviewed in the TMD article (| Article | |) (E12) and the mass-ratio selection guidance in the multiple-damper design note (TMD_nscm19.dvi) (E13).

The size is modest against the bridge and against people. A mass ratio of two and a half percent on the assumed twenty tonne modal mass gives the 500 kg TMD mass (E22), about seven body weights, and the Den Hartog tuning formulas applied in the Jordan footbridge TMD study (Control of Vibrations of Common Pedestrian Bridges in Jordan Using Tuned Mass Dampers) (E14) give 1.85 Hz tuning frequency with 9.33 percent damper damping ratio (E23), which converts to 67.8 kN/m stiffness and 1.09 kN s/m viscous coefficient (E24).

That stiffness carries the 500 kg weight with about 72.3 mm static sag, roughly a door-handle height drop, so ordinary helical steel springs plus off-the-shelf viscous dashpots can be built and carried under the deck. Not ready, because crowd force, residual acceleration and damper stroke still need a sweep before a proposal.
